title: spec review: B4b v3 (fix round of T-1491): git-state derivation WITHOUT auto-commit: every derived write (done and both holds) goes through one status-checked, registry-checked lock entry; fit_result then process; registry updated; derive default False until B5
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label B4b-v3. Respec of B4b v2 T-1529 (superseded) after spec review T-1531 request_changes; still a fix round of T-1491 (constraints.fix_round_for) so its merge stamps T-1491 and B7 T-1494 / B5 T-1511 become ready; cuts from goal/T-1403. The v2 text below is the contract; the v3 AMENDMENTS at the end override it where they differ and answer T-1531 W1-W7 verbatim. The commit-now resume stays DROPPED; auto-commit of leftovers stays PARKED as B4c.

Contract: gitutil.execute_outcome(worktree, parent, scope, *, since=None) -> {ahead, head, dirty_in_scope, dirty_out_of_scope} | None and gitutil.head_sha(worktree) are MERGED (B4a); hold prefix 'execute_incomplete' (B5 maps it to failure kind 'incomplete').

Evidence (U2, 2026-10-01): status_reason non_json is set in spawn.run_worker when json.loads of the `claude -p --output-format json` stdout fails; every recorded case is 'non-JSON output (rc=143): ' with empty output (SIGTERM); r carries only 'reason' (text[-500:]), no 'output' key. luna T-0526: the worker posted done itself through bus_post_result and reconcile marked the process dead. So the signal is the git state of the worktree, and a result the worker already posted must win.

Facts (goal/T-1403; spawn.py/worker_control.py unchanged since main 355583c): spawn.run_worker sets t['executor'] = 'claude:<tier>' before run_claude; the done path runs fit_result then contracts.process on the result and posts {'summary', 'executed_by', 'review'} with no commit; the failed path posts status failed, reason, resume_hint.partial_output. Every write goes through worker_control.write_if_current (bus lock + is_current(epoch)) which checks the epoch only, not the task status. worker_control.cancel() SIGTERMs the child (rc 143) and does NOT bump steer_epoch; registry status moves 'cancelling' -> 'cancelled'; the task is held 'cancelled' only at finish; a steer bumps steer_epoch. run_claude calls worker_registry.finish(..., 'failed', 'non_json') before returning. bus.post_result raises ValueError above MAX_RESULT_CHARS.

Change:
1. spawn.py module seams `execute_outcome = gitutil.execute_outcome`, `head_sha = gitutil.head_sha` referenced as module attributes. derive = pool.cfg.get('spawn', {}).get('derive_execute_result', False): DEFAULT FALSE until B5 (T-1511) maps execute_incomplete holds; the flip to True is a one-line follow-up after B5 merges. False -> today's behaviour exactly, and head_sha is not called at all.
2. worker_control.cancel_or_steer_pending(task_id, epoch) -> bool: True when the worker registry entry has status in {'cancelling', 'cancelled', 'steering'}, or the task is held with hold_reason 'cancelled', or not is_current(task_id, epoch); False otherwise; never raises (missing registry entry -> False).
3. run_worker, role execute only, derive True: pre_head = head_sha(worktree) wrapped in try/except -> None, before run_claude. Derivation runs ONLY when r['status'] == 'failed' AND the reason starts with 'non-JSON output' AND not cancel_or_steer_pending(task_id, epoch). Every other outcome keeps today's write; the done path never calls execute_outcome or head_sha. pre_head None on a git worktree -> today's failed write. o = execute_outcome(worktree, parent, scope, since=pre_head) wrapped in try/except -> None; None -> today's failed write (reason and partial_output kept).
4. Decision (no git mutation anywhere): (i) o['ahead'] == 0 -> hold 'execute_incomplete: no commits' with resume_hint {'partial_output', 'dirty_in_scope', 'dirty_out_of_scope', 'head'}; (ii) any dirty path -> hold 'execute_incomplete: uncommitted changes', same resume_hint shape; (iii) ahead > 0 and clean -> candidate = {'summary', 'commit': head, 'executed_by': t['executor'], 'derived_from': 'git_state', 'review': same text as the done path}, processed through the same pipeline as the done path, then posted done. bus.log_run(task, role='execute', outcome='derived_done' | 'execute_incomplete', executor=t['executor'], derived_from='git_state') exactly once per derived decision that wrote.
5. Key passthrough: contracts.process and spawn.fit_result keep 'commit', 'derived_from', 'executed_by' and 'review' (confirm by reading; if either strips unknown keys, re-attach the four after on a copy; contracts.py is out of scope).

v3 AMENDMENTS (answer T-1531; each overrides the item above where they differ):
W1 (high): ONE guarded writer for every derived outcome. worker_control.post_if_current(task_id, epoch, status, payload) -> bool: ONE bus.locked() entry that re-reads the task and the worker registry entry; returns False and writes nothing unless fresh['status'] == 'running' AND is_current(task_id, epoch) AND the registry status is not in {'cancelling', 'cancelled', 'steering'} AND not (fresh.get('result') or {}).get('commit') (the EXISTING result's commit); else writes inline (status 'done' -> bus.post_result(task_id, payload, 'done'); status 'held' -> bus.update(task_id, status='held', hold_reason=payload['hold_reason'], resume_hint=payload['resume_hint'])) and returns True. Both hold paths (4.i, 4.ii) and the derived done (4.iii) go through it; plain write_if_current is never used for a derived outcome, so a worker-posted done/held/failed always wins.
W2 (med): the registry re-check is inside post_if_current's lock (above); cancel_or_steer_pending before derivation stays as an early exit only.
W3 (med): 4.iii order is fit_result(candidate) -> contracts.process(fitted, repair_session=None) -> post_if_current(task_id, epoch, 'done', processed), exactly the done path's order; bus.post_result can therefore not raise on size.
W4 (med): after a derived outcome that wrote, run_worker updates the worker_registry entry: status_reason 'derived_done' (status 'done') or 'execute_incomplete' (status 'held'), through the registry writer run_claude uses; when post_if_current returned False the entry stays 'failed/non_json' on purpose (documented: the worker's own posting won and reconcile already handled it).
W5 (low): summary is always 'derived from git state after <reason>' and resume_hint.partial_output is the reason text (r['reason']), because the non-JSON r has no output text; tests build r exactly as run_claude returns it (reason only).
W6 (low): when post_if_current returns False, run_worker returns {'status': 'superseded'} with no failed write and no log_run entry; the output_contract decision_log row contracts.process wrote for the unposted candidate is accepted (documented in the run_worker docstring).
W7 (low): the spawn.execute_outcome / spawn.head_sha seams are patched only in the derivation TestCases (setUp of the new test class), not in every execute TestCase; derive defaults to False so legacy tests never reach them.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE): tests/test_spawn.py::test_failed_without_reason_key_sets_default_and_resume_hint passes unchanged. Cancel/steer signals in tests: registry status through the worker_control registry writer the existing tests use; steer by bumping steer_epoch; pre-posted done/held/failed by bus.update or bus.post_result before the derivation runs.

Out of scope: gitutil.py, daemon.py, executor.py, failures.py, contracts.py, pool.toml. Rollback: `git revert` of the merge, or [spawn].derive_execute_result = false (the default). Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run tests/test_spawn.py tests/test_worker_control.py in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by line number.
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_execute_result_derived_from_git_state: passes: with derive_execute_result True, run_worker for an execute task whose run_claude returns failed 'non-JSON output (rc=143): ' (reason only, no output key) (a) posts status done with result.commit = the worktree HEAD, derived_from 'git_state', executed_by = t['executor'], summary 'derived from git state after ...' and the review text present after fit_result and contracts.process, bus.log_run called exactly once with outcome 'derived_done', and the worker registry entry status_reason 'derived_done', when the run added a commit and the tree is clean; (b) with any uncommitted path, in scope or out, holds 'execute_incomplete: uncommitted changes' through post_if_current with resume_hint.dirty_in_scope/dirty_out_of_scope and partial_output = the reason text, git status unchanged, registry status_reason 'execute_incomplete'; (c) with a pre-existing commit but none since run start holds 'execute_incomplete: no commits'; (d) a run_claude 'done' result never calls execute_outcome or head_sha

tests/test_spawn.py::test_derivation_skipped_for_cancel_steer_and_legacy_cases: passes: the task is marked failed exactly as before (reason kept, partial_output kept, no derived log_run entry, registry stays failed/non_json) when derive_execute_result is False (head_sha never called), when the failed reason is not 'non-JSON output', when head_sha returns None on a git worktree, when head_sha or execute_outcome raises, when the registry status is 'cancelling', 'cancelled' or 'steering', and when steer_epoch was bumped; a task already held 'cancelled' is left untouched; when the worker already posted done, held or failed before derivation, post_if_current returns False for the done AND both hold outcomes, nothing is written, run_worker returns status 'superseded' and the registry entry stays failed/non_json

tests/test_worker_control.py::test_post_if_current_single_lock_entry: passes: worker_control.post_if_current(task_id, epoch, status, payload) enters bus.locked exactly once (patched counter), re-reads the task and the registry inside the lock, returns False and writes nothing when is_current is False, when the fresh status is 'done', 'held' or 'failed', when the registry status is cancelling/cancelled/steering, or when the EXISTING result has a commit; otherwise writes inline (post_result for 'done', bus.update held with hold_reason and resume_hint for 'held') and returns True; a payload with its own 'commit' key does not block the write; cancel_or_steer_pending returns True for registry status cancelling/cancelled/steering, for a task held 'cancelled' and for a stale epoch, False otherwise, and never raises for a missing registry entry
